pk.context: 500 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

tell: Its 12-to-17-hour half-life stays the same across formulations, which sets this NSAID apart.

clues.text: Oral bioavailability is 95%, and more than 99% of the drug is bound to albumin. About 95% of a dose is excreted in urine, mostly as conjugates.
An odorless crystalline substance with a molecular weight of 230.26.
Approved under an NDA in 250 mg, 375 mg and 500 mg strengths, usually given twice daily.
Boxed warning on serious cardiovascular thrombotic events. Contraindicated around bypass graft surgery and after asthma or urticaria from aspirin; gastrointestinal complaints are most frequent.
Relief of the signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and juvenile arthritis.
It belongs to the NSAID group, but this label describes no specific enzyme or receptor target.
The generic name begins with N and has eight letters.
